description: Continuous latency and loss monitoring for a home or small network, built for a Raspberry Pi: SmokePing probes, Grafana, alerting, and an MCP server over the recorded history.
rules: Install and operate the stack with the smoking-pi command (install, enable, alerts, config set). The command writes the env file: .env from a clone, /etc/smoking-pi/env when packaged.
Shipped probes step every 300 s (10 ICMP pings, or 5 for DNS, HTTP and TCP). An alert window has to cover more than three steps.
latency and dns_latency store loss as a 0-1 ratio; cpe_latency stores loss as 0-100 percent. DNS and HTTP medians in InfluxDB are seconds.
A flat 100% loss with no variance is a monitoring artifact: outbound ICMP is blocked, bare amazon.com does not answer ICMP (use a www host), or the host has no global IPv6.
get_chart is the only MCP tool that returns an image, and only when called. The stack keeps the MCP server on loopback (MCP_HOST=127.0.0.1).
The gateway rate-limits ICMP, so cpe_latency has a permanent loss floor. A microcut is a window above MICROCUT_LOSS_PCT (50%).
